lines: A clean return with no snags. I like a trip that ends that way.
Everyone came back standing. That is enough for me.
The road behaved for once.
We kept a good pace and still had food left at the end.
No broken gear, no missing people, and no bad surprises.
I would travel with that group again.
We chose the safer path and lost nothing but time.
The weather held until the village was in sight.
A quiet journey makes the hot meal afterward taste even better.
We crossed every stream before the rain raised them.
The packs stayed dry and nobody wandered off.
I slept well knowing the watch was taken seriously.
We reached shelter before dark each night.
The route was longer than promised, but it was sound.
Good planning made the whole trip feel shorter.
We did not need a blade, a bandage, or a desperate idea.
The boat landed where we meant it to land.
I came home with the same number of arrows I took.
That was the rare journey with nothing worth complaining about.
Safe out and safe back. Let us keep doing it that way.
Something got its hook in me out there. Next time, we cut the line sooner.
I made it back, but this wound will slow my work for a while.
We pressed on after the warning signs. That was a mistake.
The bandage held through the journey home.
I can still move every finger, which matters more to me than pride.
Next time I say I need rest, listen the first time.
The road took its payment in blood.
I should have kept my shield up instead of watching the others.
Cold rain made the injury worse before we found shelter.
I was lucky the cut missed the bone.
The group got me home, though none of us looked graceful doing it.
I will need lighter work until the swelling goes down.
We had food for the trip, but not enough clean cloth.
I learned exactly which buckle fails when someone falls on it.
The wound is ugly, not deadly.
I kept walking because stopping there would have been worse.
Someone carried my pack for the last mile. I owe them a meal.
The trip ended safely, but not cheaply.
Give me a few days and I will be useful again.
We survived. Now we should learn why it came that close.
I know bait when I see it now. Do not ask me to bite twice.
You left me exposed after promising to cover that side.
The danger was bad enough before trust failed with it.
I came home because I stopped relying on your word.
You knew the route was unsafe and kept quiet.
I will not travel under that arrangement again.
A bad knot warns you by slipping. A liar waits until you lean on them.
You took the supplies and left the rest of us hungry.
I saw who ran when the fighting started.
Do not dress betrayal up as a difficult choice.
We made plans together, then you changed yours alone.
I can forgive fear more easily than a planned lie.
The group survived in spite of what happened, not because of it.
I will count every ration myself next time.
You pointed us toward danger and kept the safe path for yourself.
Trust takes longer to mend than a torn net.
I have heard your excuse. It does not match what I saw.
Nobody gets to use my loyalty as bait again.
We can work near each other, but I will not turn my back.
That journey taught me exactly whose word holds under weight.
A boat is honest enough. It goes where it is pointed, unlike some plans.
The hull rode low, but it brought everyone across.
Whoever packed the boat forgot that wet food is useless food.
We made good time once the wind turned behind us.
The landing was rough because nobody checked the shore first.
I tied the supplies high and watched the others learn why.
The river route saved us a full day of walking.
One oar cracked halfway over, so the spare earned its place.
The boat leaked just enough to keep everyone busy.
We followed the bank until the fog lifted.
I would take that crossing again with a better weather report.
The current carried us east faster than the map suggested.
Everyone learned to sit still after the first wave came aboard.
We found a quiet cove and slept above the tide line.
The rope work was sound, even if the rowing was not.
A dolphin followed us long enough to improve the mood.
We reached the far shore with dry packs and tired arms.
The boat handled the open water better than I expected.
Next trip, we bring two oars for every pair of hands.
I trust a journey more when I can see the wake behind it.
